seeds.title: The Fast, Luminous Ultraviolet Transient AT2018cow: Extreme Supernova, or Disruption of a Star by an Intermediate-Mass Black Hole? (Perley et al. 2019)
seeds.contribution: 20 branches (17 with named rejection), 6 depth conclusions, 8 shape facts

facts.assertion: Practitioner action is publishing a cause, but as an unresolved hypothesis set (jet-driven failed SN vs IMBH TDE); no adjudicated cause exists in this seed
Rival hypotheses were weighed qualitatively across channels; only the TDE hypothesis received a quantitative forward-model fit (MOSFiT MCMC); no likelihood comparison between hypotheses
Follow-up (intervene) decision taken in real time via GROWTH marshal to filter alerts and coordinate follow-up
Object is also ZTF18abcfcoo; its cause discussion is published and indexed (contamination under explain)
X-ray and radio channels analysed in companion papers (Ho et al. 2018; Margutti et al. 2018), not in this seed
Early subset-of-channels conclusion (Ic-BL) was later overturned by further time-series data: an instance where a conclusion reached at a cut epoch was wrong
949 photometric points released machine-readable
Rival SN hypothesis ruled out by forward reasoning on light curve (Ni mass, no second peak), not by fitting a SN light-curve model

seeds.title: Supernova Photometric Classification Pipelines Trained on Spectroscopically Classified Supernovae from the Pan-STARRS1 Medium-Deep Survey (Villar et al. 2019)
seeds.contribution: 16 branches (14 with named rejection), 4 depth conclusions, 8 shape facts

facts.assertion: Label source: spectroscopic classifications via SNID template matching; SNID misclassification possible
No held-out-epoch prediction: evaluation is leave-one-out CV on complete light curves; performance on partial light curves (real-time) not evaluated
Model parameters are partly degenerate (A not peak flux, t0 not explosion/peak time; correlations listed)
Posteriors well constrained for well-sampled light curves, poorly for sparse ones; posterior draws propagate to classification uncertainty
No per-object fit-quality rejection criterion is reported; the only object cut is the detection count; authors state further information-content cuts may be necessary
Likelihood includes observational error plus a white-noise scatter term; PyMC Metropolis-Hastings
Spectroscopic follow-up magnitude limit ~1.5 mag shallower than survey depth (selective labels relative to photometric sample)
Pipeline code released on GitHub excluding the MCMC fitting step

seeds.title: The Zwicky Transient Facility Bright Transient Survey I: Spectroscopic Classification and the Redshift Completeness of Local Galaxy Catalogs (Fremling et al.)
seeds.contribution: 25 branches (22 with named rejection), 10 depth conclusions, 10 shape facts

facts.assertion: Label source: classifications are human (SNID template match plus visual inspection by named team members); TNS classifications are preliminary and subsumed by the paper
The governed action is scanners assigning scarce spectroscopic follow-up (5-15 candidates per night); only assigned objects get labels (selective labels)

Per-object published values: SN type, SNID redshift, peak time and magnitude per band, E(B-V), host name/position/redshift/photometry (Tables 1 and 3): contamination-relevant for infer on these quantities
No light-curve model is fitted: peak time and magnitude are read directly from alert photometry; no SALT or parametric fit, no forward model, no held-out-epoch prediction in this seed
Rise and fade times (0.75 mag from peak) estimated by an automated procedure only for completeness checks
Light-curve features are used as a secondary channel in classification (r-band shoulder/secondary peak)
Classification accuracy adjudicated against ePESSTO: 26 in common, 2 disagreements
SNID template set heterogeneity acknowledged as a source of sub-classification uncertainty
Selection effects: BTS incomplete for SNe near AGN; biased against slow SLSNe present in reference images
Completeness validated by re-processing all 2018 alerts with AMPEL: 17 missed SNe, 97% scanning completeness

seeds.title: Photometric Classification of 2315 Pan-STARRS1 Supernovae with Superphot (Hosseinzadeh et al. 2020)
seeds.contribution: 20 branches (16 with named rejection), 5 depth conclusions, 9 shape facts

facts.assertion: Correctness of individual test-set classifications cannot be judged (no labels); only agreement with other classifiers is measured
Per-object reduced chi2 (median-parameter model) and max Gelman-Rubin R-hat are reported for each transient
No fit-quality rejection cut is applied: Table 3 rows include reduced chi2 801.5 with R-hat 1.7 (PSc000102) and R-hat 1.8 (PSc000150) still classified
Reduced chi2 is infinite or negative when a light curve has 24 or fewer points across four filters
Bayesian modeling allows fitting part of a light curve while keeping future behavior within uncertainties; what fraction is needed is left to future work (no held-out epoch evaluation)
For rare transients a high confidence does not imply a correct classification
Test-set light curves are worse sampled than training set because brighter targets were prioritized for spectroscopy (selective labels)
Agreement between two classifiers is not an indication of correctness
Code open source on GitHub/Zenodo/PyPI; reproducing results needs seed 0

seeds.title: The Zwicky Transient Facility Bright Transient Survey. II. A Public Statistical Sample for Exploring Supernova Demographics (Perley et al.)
seeds.contribution: 30 branches (24 with named rejection), 10 depth conclusions, 10 shape facts

facts.assertion: Label source for the sample is the most recent TNS classification (public, preliminary), with listed exceptions; subtypes removed
Authors state that deciding which transients to classify involves extensive human decision-making that can bias samples (the governed intervene action and selective labels)

Per-object values (peak time/mag, rise/fade, classification, redshift, absolute mag, host properties) are published in the real-time public BTS Sample Explorer: contamination relevant for any infer item on these quantities
No light-curve model is fitted: timescales by linear interpolation; light-curve modelling deferred to future focused papers
Analysis techniques chosen to avoid human intervention
Quality cuts requiring pre-peak, near-peak and post-peak coverage remove 48% of the sample (supply of well-sampled light curves)
Spectroscopic completeness 93% at m<18.5, 97% at m<18, 75% at m<19; unclassified events mostly missed through weather (labels missing by season)
Seasonal dependence of classification success from weather
Completeness of saving checked against 4350 TNS-classified transients cross-matched to ZTF alerts
Authors expect heavy reliance on photometric classification for Rubin, with bright-end spectroscopic surveys as training data

seeds.title: SALT3: An Improved Type Ia Supernova Model for Measuring Cosmic Distances (Kenworthy et al. 2021)
seeds.contribution: 17 branches (13 with named rejection), 3 depth conclusions, 8 shape facts

facts.assertion: Model validation grader is distance-level (Hubble residual RMS, alpha/beta, Diff(dz mu)) on held-out SNe or simulated truth, not prediction of held-out epochs of individual light curves
Held-out validation design exists at study level: random half split K21train/K21valid (541/541)
Training label source: spectroscopically classified Branch-normal SNe Ia (incl. 91T-like); many training spectra are TNS classification spectra
K21 compilation contains no ZTF photometry (surveys listed: Calan-Tololo, CfA1-4, SDSS, SNLS, CSP, Foundation, PS1 MDS, DES)
SALT3.K21 is integrated in sncosmo and SNANA; training code, data, model public (forward model available to any arm)
The SED model is itself a generative forward model: F(p,lambda)=x0[M0+x1 M1]exp(c CL), integrated through bandpass at redshift
Model is SN Ia-only (single stretch parameter); authors state one SED parameter will not capture full diversity
Per-object light-curve fitting is a uniform pipeline step (SNANA fit then Tripp); no per-object model-family choice is described

seeds.title: SNIascore: Deep Learning Classification of Low-Resolution Supernova Spectra (Fremling et al.)
seeds.contribution: 17 branches (16 with named rejection), 5 depth conclusions, 9 shape facts

facts.assertion: Training, validation and testing labels are BTS classifications (manual SNID template matching plus inspection); BTS18 human-vetted; testing labels subject to minor future change
From 2021-04-15 SNIascore auto-reports SN Ia classifications and redshifts to TNS: later BTS SN Ia labels can be annotations derived from this model's output
An official BTS/TNS classification (SN 2020eyj as SN Ia) was later judged likely wrong: TNS labels are not measured truth in every case
The only use of a light-curve model is a per-object check that SN Ia light-curve models fail to match, used to reject the SN Ia class (explain-type evidence, not a published fit)
Evaluation is on held-out validation and later testing data against SNID and DASH baselines via ROC; FPR<1% is a hard requirement
Light-curve information is often unavailable at the time of the spectrum; many spectra are pre-maximum
Proposed (not practised): objects whose SNIascore changes when the light curve is included may warrant further follow-up
Spectral phase uses time of maximum from the BTS Sample Explorer brightest measurement, not a fitted model
Planned relaxed cut would remove human interaction for most BTS SNe Ia (about 80% testing, 90% validation), i.e. more than 50% of BTS SNe (body text; the abstract's 60% figure is not used)

seeds.title: ParSNIP: Generative Models of Transient Light Curves with Physics-Enabled Deep Learning (Boone 2021)
seeds.contribution: 15 branches (13 with named rejection), 4 depth conclusions, 11 shape facts

facts.assertion: Generative-model validation practised = residuals of whole held-out light curves (random 10% of objects), not forecasting later epochs of a partially observed object
Training-set residuals consistent with statistical uncertainties, author suspects overfitting; validation core dispersion ~0.06 mag
Large residuals for transient types poorly represented in training: a learned forward model as grader penalizes rare types (I4 risk)
Per-object comparison of two model families practised: median reduced chi2 1.42 (1.68) ParSNIP vs 1.40 (1.21) SALT2 on SNe Ia
SALT2 well-fit cuts used: converged fit, x1 in [-5,5], sigma_x1<0.5, sigma_c<0.1, >=1 pre-max observation
Model assumes known redshift; photo-z path not implemented in the paper (only proposed)
Preprocessing requires a stable background before and after the transient and estimates background from points >=250 d from peak, i.e. it presupposes the full light curve (bears on a cut-epoch item)
Spectra-comparison objects PS1-12cht and PS1-12baa were included in training for that run (in-sample demonstration)
Decoder claimed usable for any instrument/bandpass without modification (wave-1 tool card lists a code disagreement)
Posterior Gaussian approximation holds even for partially sampled light curves (MCMC check), no multimodality seen
Novel-transient detection is framed as needing a follow-up feedback loop that spends resources (intervene named, not practised)

seeds.title: The Zwicky Transient Facility Bright Transient Survey. III. BTSbot: Automated Identification and Follow-up of Bright Transients with Deep Learning
seeds.contribution: 23 branches (19 with named rejection), 5 depth conclusions, 10 shape facts

facts.assertion: Label source for negatives includes scanners' non-saves (rejects): labels are the historical follow-up policy itself
Practitioner action is committing spectroscopic follow-up: scanners save and request spectra
Validation of the governed decision is by simulating policies on historical candidates and comparing to scanner save/trigger times, not by outcomes of untaken actions
Scanner purity cannot be computed straightforwardly because scanners act on dim transients deliberately (selective-labels/value ambiguity)
False positives on dim SNe are judged an appropriate use of spectroscopic time: value of the action differs from the class label
BTSbot uses no redshift information
Present-day window chosen to reduce bias from BTSbot actions visible to scanners influencing their decisions (policy leakage into labels)
Task is binary classification that includes a forecast of whether the source will reach mpeak<=18.5; no light-curve model fit, no forward model, no held-out-epoch prediction practised
Scanning also involves retrieving host redshifts from NED and TNS classifications (not yet automated)
About 70% of BTS bright transients are SNe Ia; SNIascore classifies and reports 80-90% of these

seeds.title: Superphot+: Realtime Fitting and Classification of Supernova Light Curves (de Soto et al. 2024)
seeds.contribution: 26 branches (21 with named rejection), 7 depth conclusions, 15 shape facts

facts.assertion: Per-object published output: five class probabilities plus fit reduced chi2 and ALeRCE label, machine-readable on Zenodo (Table 5).
Fit parameters are saved as light-curve properties on ANTARES (a published per-object fit exists for objects processed in realtime).
Training set keeps partial light curves: 91 pre-peak-only, 503 post-peak-only; poorly sampled fits are prior-dominated.
Truncation experiment fits and classifies truncated light curves and grades by classification metrics; no prediction of held-out later photometry is evaluated anywhere in the paper.
6,061 (~99%) spectroscopic light curves pass median reduced chi2 < 1.2.
Labels come from TNS spectroscopic classifications; 66% of training light curves are also in ZTF BTS.
Priors are set from marginal posteriors of fits to the same dataset (data-derived priors).
Parametric model cannot capture SN Ia secondary r-band bumps; ParSNIP can.
Tail clipping touches 4,324 of 9,526 light curves (45%), due to template-subtraction artefacts.
Early-phase classifier outperforms full-phase before ~20 days but is not deployed on ANTARES.
ANTARES filter has not yet incorporated the early-phase variant.
SuperRAENN decodings of the same encoding vary with number of requested timestamps (forward-model instability of an alternative generator).
Internal disagreement: binary SN Ia threshold p>=0.142 (Fig. 13 caption) vs p=0.175 (Sec. 5.3 text).
sigma_extra per band added in quadrature to account for empirical model limitations.
Fits from light curves with only rise or decline information are more likely prior-dominated.

seeds.title: ATAT: Astronomical Transformer for time series And Tabular data
seeds.contribution: 13 branches (12 with named rejection), 4 depth conclusions, 6 shape facts

facts.assertion: All training and evaluation are on simulated ELAsTiCC data; labels are simulation truth; authors warn real LSST performance may differ
Metadata channel includes host spectroscopic/photometric redshift and MW extinction
Grader is an answer key: held-out test set of 1000 light curves per class
The only forward-model fit (SPM) is a feature extractor with tuned bounds; fit quality is never graded on held-out epochs
Early classification evaluated on light curves truncated at days after first alert (partial light curves), graded against class labels
Practitioner action: model put into production in the ALeRCE broker (tool built; per-object outputs are class predictions)

seeds.title: ZTF SN Ia DR2: Overview (Rigault, Smith et al. 2024/2025)
seeds.contribution: 14 branches (8 with named rejection), 3 depth conclusions, 10 shape facts

facts.assertion: Per object DR2 publishes SALT2 t0, x0, x1, c with errors and covariances, fitprob, coverage and fit-quality flags, redshift, type and subtype: a published fit exists for every released DR2 SN Ia
Released forced-photometry g,r,i light curves for 3591 SNe Ia plus 5138 spectra; also on WISeREP
Extra tables publish alternative per-object fits: SALT2.4 or SALT3 templates, alternative phase windows, with or without i band
Label source: spectroscopic classification, snid matching plus crowd visual vetting (each SN vetted at least twice), experts on edge cases
79% of DR2 targets are covered by the BTS program (overlap with BTS supply)
Light-curve model accuracy (fit residuals) and an extra stretch-like parameter are studied in companion papers (Rigault 2024b, Kenworthy 2024); not in this seed
Photometry has percent-level nonlinearity (pocket effect) after Nov 2019; zero point known at 5%
Light curves of 37 normal SNe Ia at z<0.015 withheld for an H0 program
Typical sampling: ~40 detections in [-10,+40], median 9 pre-max and 27 post-max; detected 12 d before max
Spectroscopic follow-up selection modelled as sigmoid with m0=18.8, matching BTS completeness

non_seed_inputs_read: fm-advantage-benchmark-with-shape: SKILL.md, references/shape.md, manifest.md, provenance.md, loop.md, graph.md, references/stages/discovery.md, references/stages/supply.md, schemas/domain_manifest.schema.json, scripts/validate.py
reading_method: Each seed downloaded fresh from arxiv.org/pdf/<id> (id verified against the PDF header), pdftotext -layout; read L1 to last line in chunks including references. 2109.13999 read by agent 1; the other 11 by five reading forks of agent 1 under one written rule set; every quote verified by script (0 failures on 452 quotes); agent 1 re-read 15 ruling-bearing locators in 7 seeds against the layout text.
completeness: 12 seeds, all read in full, all ids verified by download, none wrong. Held full texts from earlier waves were not reused for locators because wave-1 agent 4 read from a copy with numeric table cells stripped; fresh downloads were used instead. Not read: DR2 companion fitting papers, AT2018cow X-ray/radio companions, SuperRAENN, SALT3 F22 recalibration (Brout et al. 2022).
